sense: following the length of: along the river, along the road

terms.gloss: along, alongside (a river, a coast, a road)
evidence: Plaut. Rud. 148–149: quid illūc est … hominum secundum lītus?
Cic. Att. 16.8.2: iter secundum mare superum faciunt
terms.comment: Following the line of a thing, beside it: secundum flūmen, along the river; secundum lītus, along the shore. Its other senses, after and in keeping with: see according to.

terms.grammar: ablative of the way, without a preposition
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā
terms.comment: The road one goes by stands in the ablative: viā Sacrā īre, go along the Sacred Way (see via). Per viam, through the street, is also said.

evidence: Caes. BG 1.48.2: praeter castra Caesaris suās cōpiās trādūxit
terms.comment: Along and past a thing: see past.

phrases.latin: Prō dī immortālēs, quid illūc est, Scēparniō, hominum secundum lītus?
phrases.english: Good heavens, Sceparnio, who are those people over there along the shore?

phrases.latin: hieme cum hībernant secundum mare, aestū abiguntur in montēs frondōsōs
phrases.english: in winter they winter along the sea; in the heat they are driven up into the leafy mountains

phrases.latin: an īret ad trīs legiōnēs Macedonicās quae iter secundum mare superum faciunt
phrases.english: or whether to go to the three Macedonian legions that are marching along the Adriatic coast

phrases.latin: ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs, nescio quid meditāns nūgārum, tōtus in illīs
phrases.english: I happened to be walking along the Sacred Way, as is my habit, thinking over some trifle or other, quite lost in it
